questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Rich cultural life and a good university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic burden was too large. We attended school from morning to afternoon all week days while sometimes having to wake up at 6 to study before school and not go to bed until 2 am just to get through a regular week. This is due to the fact that we attended 6 courses when the trimester was designed to take 4, as this was the only way we could achieve 30 ECTS. However, this was not information that was available to us before we applied and got accepted into the university. If we had known, we would have selected another university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Medium. A bit too many different places to find information, but it all worked out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were able to talk to someone at the university that helped us.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We were four girls, so it was easy to find apartments through airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: We rented three different apartments through airbnb. That worked really well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not try it,

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We showed up and handed the papers to them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Several employees at the university was there at the registration process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We wrote down our requests with the guidance of the employees present at registration - and got into all our classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: High academic level in most courses. Our lecturers were recognized and many had had their worked published.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not as technological. We often had to make very costly print outs, some courses did not have slides, and exams were in hand. Besides that it varied. We were very few in each class. Some demanded that we participated a lot, some just taught by the board.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economic Growth II, Regional and Urban Economics, Empirical Methods in Regional and Urban Economics, Cooperative Decision Making and Social Choice, Political Economy, Governments and Markets.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economic Growth II and Cooperative Decision Making and Social Choice. Detailed explanation of theories and literature and skilled lecturers.

questions.answer: Alcohol and transportation was cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do not really know.. We found all of those ourselves.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction day, where we met some tutors (mine however, did not contact our group until November), who on two occasions showed us the Bunkers del Carmen and some local bars. We did not hear of any athletic events. Through Erasmus, there were cultural and social events - but I did not find any at our host institution.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Through the host institution? I did not try any.
On our own, we found a lot though. I would really recommend hiking in Mont Rebei, taking a day trip to Sietges and many others.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Placa del Sol in Gracia, sunset at Bunkers del Carmen, bar hopping at passeig del born.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: We mostly met other exchange students from around the world.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Perhaps the sense of time. The meeting time might not be so strict. Moreover, more people than expected did not speak english.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Staying out late, gathering in small groups in the streets outside bars bringing life to the streets.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Find 3-4 people to rent an airbnb together with. It sounds like we lived cheaper than other students.
- Attend the introduction day, we met many people there.
- Attend the Erasmus Events, especially in the beginning to get to know people. Especially then, people are very open to meet new friends

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: i can not think of more.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just living, enjoying the sun, having fun.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding time enough to get through the studies.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
